# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 28 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 36 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_028_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 28

**1** Jesus said: "I took my stand [аие маатоі] in the midst [тмнте] of the world [космос], and in the flesh [сарx] I appeared [оуонхт] to them.

**2** I found all of them drunk [тохе]. I found none of them thirsty [очте].

**3** And my soul [юхн] was pained [коне] for the children of humanity, because they are blind [вал] in their heart [хнт] and do not see that they have come into the world [космос] empty [шоуеіт], and they seek to go out of the world [космос] empty.

**4** But now they are drunk. When they shake off their wine [нрп], then they will repent [метаноі]."

---

**Textual Notes (EMET):**
- *сарx*: flesh; Greek loan-word — the incarnation language
- *оуонхт*: appeared, was manifested; the same revelation-vocabulary as throughout Thomas
- *тохе*: drunk, intoxicated; cf. Saying 13 (Thomas drunk from the spring)
- *очте*: thirst; the paradox — drunk but not thirsty; they have the wrong satisfaction
- *юхн*: soul; Jesus has a soul that grieves
- *коне*: to ache, grieve, be in pain; strong emotional language
- *шоуеіт*: empty, hollow; they arrive and depart empty
- *метаноі*: to repent; Greek loan-word μετάνοια — a change of mind/direction
- *нрп*: wine; when they sober up from their worldly intoxication
